source.title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory

accepted.question_text: Let A be a subset of the real numbers, and define I(A) to be the set of gauge functions f such that the Hausdorff measure H^f(A) is positive. Determine the possible complexity and set-theoretic behavior of the map A ↦ I(A): (1) does the range of I have the same cardinality as 2^R; (2) for closed sets C, the set I(C) is arithmetic (Σ^0_2), but what is the complexity of the set of Σ^0_2 formulas φ such that φ defines I(C) for some closed set C, and is this set Σ^1_2-complete; (3) is the statement that the Borel hierarchy is proper with respect to the range of I independent of ZFC; and (4) is it consistent with ZFC that whenever H^f(A) > 0 there is a subset A0 of A such that H^f(A0) is finite and positive?

evidence.quote: Given A ⊆ R. Define I(A) = {f gauge function : Hf(A) > 0}.

Problem 1. Natural questions about A 7→ I(A): (1) Does the range of I have the same cardinality as 2R? ... (2) ... What’s the complexity of the set {Σ0_2 formula φ : φ defines an I(C) for some C}? Is it Σ1_2-complete? ... (3) Is the answer to 'Borel hierarchy is proper w.r.t. the range of I' independent of ZFC? (4) Is it consistent with ZFC that for every f and A ⊆ R, if Hf(A) > 0, then there is a subset A0 such that Hf(A0) is finite and positive?

accepted.question_text: For a real x, let L_x = {z : z ≤^+_K x} and U_x = {z : z ≥_K x}. Is it true that (1) L_x is countable exactly when lim inf_n→∞ (K(x↾n) − K(n)) < ∞, and (2) U_x is countable exactly when lim inf_n→∞ (K(n) + n − K(x↾n)) < ∞?

evidence.quote: Problem 2. Let Lx = {z : z ≤+_K x} and Ux = {z : z ≥K x}. Are the following true? (1) Lx is countable iff lim infn→∞(K(x ↾ n) − K(n)) < ∞; (2) Ux is countable iff lim infn→∞(K(n) + n − K(x ↾ n)) < ∞.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the following statements hold: (1) for every computably enumerable set A, there is a computably enumerable set D ⊆ 2^N such that A ≡_rK D and both conditional plain complexities C(A↾n | D↾n) and C(D↾n | A↾n) are O(1); and (2) for every real x, there is a random real z such that z ≥_rK x, or at least z ≥_K x.

evidence.quote: Problem 3. Are the following true? (1) For any c.e. set A, there exists a c.e. set D ⊆ 2N, such that A ≡rK D and C(A ↾ n|D ↾ n) = C(D ↾ n|A ↾ n) = O(1); (2) For all x, there is a random z such that z ≥rK x (or z ≥K x).

accepted.question_text: Fix k ≥ 2. In the Even Number Game G_k, Player 1 chooses a set A of k natural numbers none of which she has played before, then Player 2 chooses an even number between min(A) and max(A), inclusive, that he has not played before; Player II loses when he has no legal move. It is known that Player 1 wins for k = 2 and k = 3. For k ≥ 4, does Player 1 have a winning strategy in G_k?

evidence.quote: Given a natural number k ≥ 2, the game Gk is a game with two players who take turns to play natural numbers. Player 1 plays a set A of k integers ... then Player 2 plays an even number between min(A) and max(A) ... Player II loses when he has no legal moves.
It was shown in [1] that for k = 2, 3, Player 1 has a winning strategy in the game Gk. For k ≥ 4, this is unknown. Problem 4. For k ≥ 4, does Player 1 have a winning strategy in the game Gk?

accepted.question_text: Let WF be the set of well-founded trees on ω and UB the set of trees on ω having a unique infinite branch. Saint Raymond proved that (WF, UB) is a coanalytic complete pair by descriptive-set-theoretic methods, and Goh proved using recursion theory that every coanalytic separator of WF and UB is coanalytic complete, which also yields Saint Raymond's theorem. Can the latter result be proved using descriptive-set-theoretic methods instead of recursion theory?
accepted.context_brief: Coanalytic separators of WF and UB

evidence.quote: Recall that WF is the collection of all well-founded trees on ω and UB is the collection of all trees on ω which have a unique infinite branch.

Using recursion theory, Goh proved that any coanalytic separator of WF and UB is coanalytic complete. The method also proves Saint Raymond’s theorem. Problem 5. Can this be proved using Descriptive Set Theoretic methods?

accepted.question_text: For a real x, define Ω^x = Σ_{σ∈2^{<ω}} 2^{-K^x(σ)}, where K^x(σ) = min{|τ| : U^x(τ) = σ}. Is there an x such that Ω^x computes 0''?

evidence.quote: Problem 6 (Downey–Hirschfeldt–Miller–Nies [1]). Is there an x such that Ωx ≥T 0′′ where Ωx = Σσ∈2<ω 2−Kx(σ) and Kx(σ) = min{|τ| : Ux(τ) = σ}?

accepted.question_text: Velickovic and Woodin proved that if A is a Σ^1_1 set with sup{ω_1^{CK(x)} : x ∈ A} = ω_1, then for every γ there exist x_0, x_1, x_2, x_3 in A such that γ ≤_h x_0 ⊕ x_1 ⊕ x_2 ⊕ x_3. Determine whether (a) there is a recursion-theoretic proof of this theorem, and (b) more generally, if A is a Σ^1_1(y) set and there is x ∈ A with ω_1^{CK(x)} > ω_1^{CK(y)}, must the Velickovic–Woodin conclusion hold for A?

evidence.quote: Theorem 8 (Velickovic–Woodin [2]). If A is Σ1_1 and sup{ωCK(x)_1 : x ∈ A} = ω1, then ∀γ∃x0, x1, x2, x3 ∈ A, γ ≤h x0 ⊕ x1 ⊕ x2 ⊕ x3.

Problem 9. (a) Is there a recursion theoretical proof for the above theorem of Velickovic–Woodin? (b) Is the following true: For any Σ1_1(y) set A, if there is x ∈ A such that ωCK(x)_1 > ωCK(y)_1, then the Velickovic–Woodin theorem holds for A?

accepted.question_text: Let T ⊆ 2^{<ω} be a positive tree, meaning that [T] has positive measure. Let P^− be the statement that every positive tree has infinitely many distinct paths, and let P be the statement that every positive tree has a perfect subtree. Over RCA_0, does P^− imply P?

evidence.quote: A tree T ⊆ 2<ω is positive if [T] has measure > 0. Consider the following statements: ... P: For every positive tree T, there is a subtree S ⊆ T which is perfect. P−: For every positive tree there are distinct (Xn : n ∈ ω) such that Xn ∈ [T].
Problem 10. Is it true that RCA0 ⊢ P− → P?

accepted.question_text: Formulate the positive-tree principles obtained by replacing measure with dimension in the definitions of P^+, P, and P^−. How do the implication and non-implication results for these principles change in that dimension-based setting?

evidence.quote: Problem 11. How about using dimension? (Define the above concepts by replacing measure by dimension.)

accepted.question_text: For the finite Ramsey-type principles FRT^e_k(Σ_{n+1}), determine whether IΣ_{n+1} + WPHP(Σ_{n+1}) proves FRT^2_2(Σ_{n+1}), and whether FRT^2_2(Σ_{n+1}) implies FRT^2_3(Σ_{n+1}).
accepted.context_brief: Finite Ramsey principles and weak pigeonhole

evidence.quote: Problem 12. IΣn+1+WPHP(Σn+1) ⊢ FRT2_2(Σn+1)? FRT2_2(Σn+1) ⊢ FRT3_2(Σn+1)?

accepted.question_text: The first-order theory 2-RAN lies strictly between CARD(Σ_2) and WPHP(Σ_2). Determine the relationship between GPHP(Σ_2) and 2-RAN: for example, which of these principles implies the other, if either does, and whether they are comparable.

evidence.quote: Problem 13. The first-order theory 2-RAN is between CARD(Σ2) and WPHP(Σ2), but how about GPHP(Σ2) and 2-RAN?

accepted.question_text: Suppose L is a finitely generated group with Π^0_1 word problem that is effectively residually finite in the sense of Theorem 14. Investigate the following: (a) can such a group have unsolvable word problem; (b) is there a finitely generated residually finite Π-group that is not effectively residually finite; and (c) Morozov constructed a Π-group not isomorphic to a subgroup of S_rec, and can one build such a group so that it is also residually finite?

evidence.quote: A f.g. group S = Fk/N is effectively residually finite (e.r.f.) if there is an algorithm that, on input w ∈ Fk, in case w /∈ N computes a finite group Q and homomorphism r : Fk → Q such that r(N) = {e} and r(w) ≠ e.

Problem 15. (a) Can such a group L have unsolvable word problem? (b) Is there a f.g., residually finite Π-group that is not effectively r.f.? (c) Morozov ... constructed a Π-group that is not isomorphic to a subgroup of Srec. Can we make such a group r.f.?

accepted.question_text: For each left-Σ^0_2 real r in [0,1], there is a computable profinite group together with a computable subgroup of Hausdorff dimension r. Which values of r can still occur if the ambient profinite group G is additionally required to be topologically finitely generated?

evidence.quote: For each left Σ2 real r ∈ [0, 1] there is a computable profinite group and computable subgroup with Hausdorff dimension r. Problem 16. Which values can occur for r when G is also topologically finitely generated?

accepted.question_text: For a first-order sentence φ in the language of groups, determine the descriptive or algorithmic complexity of the class {G : G |= φ} when G ranges over profinite groups.
accepted.context_brief: Complexity of first-order classes of profinite groups

evidence.quote: Problem 17. For a f.o. sentence φ, what is the possible complexity of {G : G |= φ}?

accepted.question_text: Is there a Borel class of profinite groups whose isomorphism relation lies strictly between smooth equivalence relations and S_∞-complete equivalence relations under Borel reducibility, and in particular does this happen in the abelian case?

evidence.quote: Problem 18. Is there some Borel class of profinite groups with isomorphism relation properly between S∞-complete and smooth? In particular, how about the Abelian case? Update: The answer to this problem is yes.

accepted.question_text: Nies, Schlicht, and Tent showed that topological isomorphism of oligomorphic groups is Borel reducible to E_∞. Is that isomorphism relation actually smooth?

evidence.quote: Problem 19. Nies, Schlicht, and Tent proved in 2019 [2] that the topological isomorphism of oligomorphic groups is ≤B E∞. Is it smooth?

accepted.question_text: If G is an oligomorphic group, must the outer automorphism group Out(G) always be profinite?
accepted.context_brief: Outer automorphism groups of oligomorphic groups

evidence.quote: Problem 21. If G is oligomorphic, is Out(G) always profinite?

accepted.question_text: Is there a Borel invariant class C of closed subgroups of S_∞ such that the isomorphism relation on C is not Borel reducible below graph isomorphism? More strongly, can one get an analytic-complete isomorphism relation in this way? The paper asks this in particular for the class of pro-countable groups.

evidence.quote: Problem 22. Is there a Borel, invariant class C of closed subgroups of S∞ with isomorphism relation not Borel below graph isomorphism? Analytic complete? How about the class C of pro-countable groups?

accepted.question_text: In the implication chain 1-generic Δ^0_2 ⇒ index guessable ⇒ computes no maximal tower ⇒ low, are the first implication and the second implication reversible?

evidence.quote: the authors showed the following implications 1-generic ∆0_2 ⇒ index guessable ⇒ computes no maximal tower ⇒ low
Problem 23. In the above diagram, are the first and the second implications reversible?

accepted.question_text: Every degree of decidable categoricity is a degree of categoricity. Is the converse true: must every degree of categoricity also occur as a degree of decidable categoricity? The paper notes in particular the cases of degrees at or above 0^(α) for large computable ordinals α, and asks what happens for d.c.e. degrees.

evidence.quote: Problem 24. Every degree of decidable categoricity is a degree of categoricity. Is the converse true? A conjecture for this problem is that it is true for d ≥ 0(α), where α is 'sufficiently large' computable ordinal. Say, for α = ω. What happens with d.c.e. degrees d?

accepted.question_text: Let Diag be the class of Turing degrees d such that every computably enumerable equivalence relation E ≠ Id_1 admits a d-computable diagonal function g with g(x) not E-equivalent to x for all x. Determine (i) the class Diag; (ii) the reverse-mathematical strength of the statement that every Σ^0_1-definable equivalence relation E ≠ Id_1 has a diagonal function; and (iii) the Weihrauch degree of the associated problem.

evidence.quote: Ceer stands for computably enumerable equivalence relation on ω. A diagonal function (or a fixed-point-free function) for a ceer E is a total function g(x) satisfying ¬g(x)Ex for all x ∈ ω.
Problem 25. The following are three versions of this problem. (i) Describe the class Diag containing those Turing degrees d such that every ceer E ̸= Id1 admits a d-computable diagonal function.

(ii) What is the reverse-mathematical strength of the statement 'Every Σ0_1-definable equivalence relation E ̸= Id1 has a diagonal function'? (iii) What is the Weihrauch degree of the corresponding problem?

accepted.question_text: Does every effectively compact left-c.e. Polish space have a computable Polish presentation whose metric is right-c.e.?

evidence.quote: Problem 26. Does every (effectively) compact left-c.e. Polish space have a computable (right c.e.) Polish copy?

accepted.question_text: Is there an infinite computable Polish space that is topologically computably categorical, meaning that any two computable presentations of that space are computably homeomorphic?

evidence.quote: A computable Polish space X is α-categorical if ... there is an α-computable homeomorphism ... X is (topologically) computably categorical if it is 0-categorical.
Problem 27. Is there an infinite computable Polish space that is topologically computably categorical?

accepted.question_text: Does Baire space have a degree of topological categoricity?

evidence.quote: Problem 28. Does the Baire space have a degree of categoricity?

accepted.question_text: Is every computably enumerable degree, or at least some computably enumerable degree, realized as the degree of topological categoricity of a computable Polish space?

evidence.quote: Problem 29. Is every/any c.e. degree the degree of topological categoricity?

accepted.question_text: Let M satisfy RCA_0 + BΣ_n + ¬IΣ_n. Fix a Π_n subset X of M, and let ⟨A_s : s ∈ M⟩ be a sequence of pairwise disjoint M-finite sets with A_s ∩ X nonempty for every s. Must there exist a function definable in M that chooses an element of A_s ∩ X for each s?

evidence.quote: Let M be a model satisfying RCA0 + BΣn + ¬IΣn. Fix a Πn subset X of M and assume ⟨As : s ∈ M⟩ is a sequence of pairwise disjoint M-finite sets such that ∀s (As ∩ X ̸= ∅).
Problem 30. Is there a definable in M choice function f of ⟨As⟩, i.e., f(s) ∈ As ∩ X?

accepted.question_text: Let M be a model, let T be a tree that is Π^0_1(∅') in M, and suppose there is a path g through T such that M[g] satisfies BΣ_2. Must there also exist a path h through T that is definable in M and still satisfies M[h] |= BΣ_2?

evidence.quote: Problem 31. Consider a tree T which is Π0_1(∅′) in M. Assume there is a g ∈ [T] such that M[g] |= BΣ2. Is there a definable path h ∈ [T] such that M[h] |= BΣ2?

accepted.question_text: For countable graphs G on ω, consider the property that G is isomorphic to its complement G^c. Is the set {G ∈ 2^{ω×ω} : G is a graph on ω and G ≅ G^c} Borel?

evidence.quote: Problem 32. Is the set {G ∈ 2ω×ω : G is a graph on ω and G ∼= Gc} Borel? ... The problem was solved during the workshop. Theorem 33 ... The set {G ∈ 2ω×ω : G is a graph on ω and G ∼= Gc} is Σ1_1-complete.

accepted.question_text: Let E be a countable Borel equivalence relation such that E = ⋃_n F_n, where each F_n is hyperfinite and F_n ⊆ F_{n+1}. Must E itself be hyperfinite?

evidence.quote: Problem 35 (The union problem). If E is a countable Borel equivalence relation and E = ∪nFn, where Fn is hyperfinite and Fn ⊆ Fn+1 for each n ∈ ω, is it true that E is hyperfinite?

accepted.question_text: Call a countable Borel equivalence relation E hyperfinite-over-hyperfinite (hf/hf) if there is a Borel partial order ≤ on its space X such that x ≤ y implies x E y, and the restriction of ≤ to each E-class is a suborder of Z^2. If E is hf/hf, must E be hyperfinite?

evidence.quote: we call a countable Borel equivalence relation hyperfinite-over-hyperfinite (or shortly, hf/hf) if there is a Borel partial order ≤ on X such that (i) if x ≤ y, then xEy, (ii) the order type of ≤↾[x] is a suborder of Z2.
Problem 37 (The hf/hf problem). If E is hf/hf, is it hyperfinite?

accepted.question_text: Assume there exists a counterexample to the hf/hf problem, that is, an hf/hf countable Borel equivalence relation that is not hyperfinite. Would it follow that the set of all hyperfinite equivalence relations is Σ^1_2-complete?

evidence.quote: Problem 39. Suppose there is a counterexample to the hf/hf problem. Is the set of all hyperfinite equivalence relations Σ1_2-complete?

accepted.question_text: Is every orbit equivalence relation arising from a Borel action of a countable amenable group hyperfinite?

evidence.quote: Problem 40 (Weiss’ question). Is the orbit equivalence relation of Borel action of countable amenable group hyperfinite?

accepted.question_text: Are the connectedness equivalence relations of graphs of uniform subexponential growth hyperfinite, where uniform subexponential growth means growth bounded by exp(r^c) for some 0 < c < 1?

evidence.quote: Problem 41. How about graphs of uniform subexponential growth, i.e., of growth less than exp(r^c) for some 0 < c < 1?

accepted.question_text: Let Act(F_∞,([0,1], λ)) be the space of measure-preserving actions of the free group F_∞ on the Lebesgue probability space, and for x in this space let Sch(x) be the Schreier graph of the action. Is the set of actions whose Schreier graph admits a measurable perfect matching Σ^1_1-complete?
accepted.context_brief: Measurable perfect matchings in Schreier graphs

evidence.quote: Problem 42. Is the set {x ∈ Act(F∞,([0, 1], λ)) : Sch(x) has a measurable perfect matching} Σ1_1-complete?

accepted.question_text: Characterize those measure-preserving automorphisms T of ([0,1], λ) for which there exists another measure-preserving automorphism S with T = S^2 = S ∘ S. The paper also records the conjecture that the set of such T is Σ^1_1-complete.

evidence.quote: Problem 43 (Halmos, 1956). What T ∈ Aut([0, 1], λ) has S ∈ Aut([0, 1], λ) with T = S^2 = S ◦ S? Conjecture: {T ∈ Aut([0, 1], λ) : ∃S ∈ Aut([0, 1], λ) T = S^2} is Σ1_1-complete.

accepted.question_text: If ⃗G is a Borel locally finite directed graph whose indegrees are uniformly bounded and whose out-neighborhoods have polynomial growth, is the connectedness equivalence relation of ⃗G hyperfinite?

evidence.quote: Problem 44. If G⃗ is a Borel locally finite directed graph whose in-degrees are uniformly bounded and out-neighborhoods have polynomial growth, is the connected equivalence relation of G⃗ hyperfinite?

accepted.question_text: Let α be a free, probability-measure-preserving, ergodic action of F_2 on a measure space (X, μ). Determine whether (i) for each nonidentity x in F_2 there is another free p.m.p. action β with the same orbit equivalence relation E_α = E_β and such that x acts ergodically in β, and (ii) there is a free p.m.p. action β with the same orbit relation in which every nontrivial element of F_2 acts ergodically.

evidence.quote: Problem 45. Let α be a free, probability measure preserving (p.m.p.) and ergodic action of F2 on measure space (X, µ). (i) If e ̸= x ∈ F2, is there a free, p.m.p action β such that Eα = Eβ and x acts ergodically? (ii) (Miller–Tserunyan). Is there a free, p.m.p action β such that every nontrivial element of F2 acts ergodically?

accepted.question_text: For every Borel ideal I on ω, does there exist a closed I-MED, that is, a closed maximal eventually different family relative to I?

evidence.quote: Let I be an ideal on ω. We can define I-MED analogous to the above definition. A family ε ⊆ ωω is called an I-MED if: (i) For all f ̸= g ∈ ε, {n : f(n) = g(n)} ∈ I and (ii) ∀h ∈ ωω∃f ∈ ε {n : f(n) = g(n)} ∈ I+.
Problem 48. For all Borel I, is there a closed I-MED?

accepted.question_text: If I is a maximal ideal on ω, does there exist a closed I-MED? The paper notes that for this problem it is enough to find a Borel I-MED.

evidence.quote: Problem 49. For maximal ideal I, is there a closed I-MED? For these problems, it is enough to find a Borel I-MED.
